failed_prediction: A held permit was assumed harmless on a cancellation edge because state would clear at the edge and downstream priority would mask all lower-priority consumers.
missing_information: The original evidence did not observe ready, drain_complete and accepted architectural side effects when an already-held permit collided with a feedback-free ROB-head-trap cancellation while raw drain and control-ready stayed high.
falsifiable_question: With a held exact-one permit and raw drain/control-ready high, does a feedback-free high-priority cancel force ready_o=0 and drain_complete_o=0 in the current cycle while the ROB-head trap is accepted exactly once?

acquisition_plan.action: Model self-consuming clear and externally sourced kill as separate causal edges; never feed a drain-derived complete clear into readiness, and always include a held-state collision test.

validation_plan.cheapest_discriminating_experiment: Run the focused held-permit+cancel tuple and the serialized-owner held-permit+ROB-head-trap integration tuple once, then delete the current-cycle ready gate in a compile-success mutation.
validation_plan.success_criterion: Production shows ready=0, drain=0, mem trap accepted once, pending arch request=0 and C1/C2 clear/no-repeat; the gate-deletion mutation compiles and is rejected.
validation_plan.counterexample: Any held-cancel cycle exposes ready or drain, accepts a lower-priority side effect, or the gate-deletion mutation passes.
